candidates.summary: the rewrite covers only href and src, so every realm's $help page publishes the crawl-time http://127.0.0.1:<port> origin
candidates.failure_scenario: Seeds() adds u+"$help" for every realm, so every preview captures one. gnoweb builds that page's function form from buildHelpURL (components/view_action.go:73 = data.Origin + pkgPath + "$help&func="), and handler_http.go:390 sets Origin = requestOrigin(r) — the scheme+host the crawler dialled, i.e. http://127.0.0.1:8899. attrRe at crawl.go:40 matches only href and src, and action.html puts that URL in form action= (line 104) and data-copy-text-value= (line 84). A reviewer who fills in the args form on the published preview and submits it navigates to http://127.0.0.1:8899/... (connection refused on their machine), and the "Copy function link" button copies that same localhost URL. mapURL would not save either attribute anyway: it returns raw untouched for anything not starting with "/".
candidates.verify_by: go test -run TestSnapshotKeepsCrawlTimeOrigin ./... in misc/gnopreview with tests/b2-lines-r2-help-origin_test.go: crawl a $help body shaped like action.html against an httptest server, write the snapshot, assert the server host does not survive
candidates.evidence: FAIL. The written r/x/y/_t/help/index.html holds: action="http://127.0.0.1:43095/r/x/y$help&func=Foo" and data-copy-text-value="http://127.0.0.1:43095/r/x/y$help&func=Foo", while the sibling href on the same page was rewritten to ../../../../../r/x/y/_t/source/. Grep evidence: handler_http.go:390 `gnourl.Origin = requestOrigin(r)`; view_action.go:73 `url.WriteString(data.Origin + pkgPath + "$help&func=" + fn.Name)`; action.html:104 `action="{{ buildHelpURL $data . }}"`.

candidates.summary: TestRewriteAddsNoindex is the only test over rewrite() and asserts nothing about the URL rewrite it exists to perform
candidates.failure_scenario: rewrite() does two jobs: inject noindex and relativize every URL. The test asserts only the first — it counts robots metas on four bodies and never looks at an attribute. No test anywhere writes a page and asserts the result carries no crawl-time origin and no absolute gnoweb path. That is exactly the gap the $help form action falls through; a one-line assertion that the written body contains neither c.Base nor a bare \"/r/\" would have caught it and would catch the next attribute gnoweb adds.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'href\|src\|action\|c.Base' misc/gnopreview/crawl_test.go between lines 167 and 194: no hit, the test body only counts noindexTag and robots metas

candidates.summary: io.ReadAll with no limit and no byte budget anywhere: -max-pages bounds the page count, nothing bounds the bytes
candidates.failure_scenario: get() reads every response whole with io.ReadAll and Run() keeps every body in c.pages until Write(). The PR under preview is what decides those bodies: a realm whose Render() emits a large page, or a $source page of a large changed file, is read into memory, held for the life of the run, and written into the uploaded artifact. grep for LimitReader|MaxBytes|ContentLength|maxSize over misc/gnopreview returns nothing, so the only backstop is -max-pages (400) — a count, not a size. The README quotes 22.2 MB / 243 pages as the shape it has seen, which is the measurement of one run, not a bound.
candidates.verify_by: grep -rnE 'LimitReader|MaxBytes|ContentLength|maxSize|max-size' misc/gnopreview — expect a byte cap, observe none; then confirm the only cap flag is -max-pages at main.go:74

candidates.summary: waitReady wraps cmd.Wait()'s error with %w, and a gnodev that exits 0 sends nil, so the diagnostic prints %!w(<nil>)
candidates.failure_scenario: startGnodev (main.go:198-203) does `died <- cmd.Wait()`, which is nil when gnodev exits with status 0 — a bad flag it rejects cleanly, a `local` subcommand that prints usage and returns. waitReady then returns fmt.Errorf("gnodev exited before serving %s — see the gnodev log: %w", probe, nil), which renders as "... see the gnodev log: %!w(<nil>)". The channel was added, per its own comment, so a gnodev that dies on startup reports why; the clean-exit case is the one where it reports garbage instead.
candidates.verify_by: fmt.Errorf("x: %w", error(nil)) in a scratch main: expect a usable message, observe "x: %!w(<nil>)"

candidates.summary: the cssRe replacement rebuilds url(...) without the quotes it matched, so a rewritten asset path that needs quoting becomes invalid CSS
candidates.failure_scenario: cssRe (line 41) matches an optional quote — `url\(\s*"?(/public/[^)"']*)"?\s*\)` — and the replacement at line 361 always emits `url(` + up + path + `)`. A stylesheet that wrote url("/public/fonts/My Font.woff2") comes back as url(../public/fonts/My Font.woff2), which is not a valid unquoted CSS url token; the browser drops the declaration and the asset silently does not load. Keeping sub-match's quoting, or always emitting double quotes, costs one concatenation.
candidates.verify_by: read crawl.go:41 and 359-362: the regex captures the quote as optional and the replacement never re-emits it

candidates.failure_scenario: setNoindex falls back to headRe when no robots meta is present, and gnoweb's layouts ship `<header class="b-header">` (components/layouts/header.html:5) on every page. A body served without a <head> — the fragment case crawl_test.go:175 says it is defending — has its noindex meta inserted inside the <header> element instead of the document head, where it is not a head meta at all. `<head[\s>]` matches the real tag and not the other one.
candidates.verify_by: regexp `(?i)<head[^>]*>` against `<header class="b-header">`: expect no match, observe a match on `<header class="b-header">`

dropped.summary: copyTree's blanket /public/ -> up rewrite inside .js breaks index.js's dynamic controller import, which resolves against the document rather than the script
dropped.settled_by: read gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/public/js/index.js: the prefix `a="/public/js/controller-"` is consumed by `s=import(i)`, and a dynamic import() specifier resolves against the referencing script's URL, so ../js/controller-x.js from public/js/index.js lands on public/js/controller-x.js. copyTree's up for rel=js/index.js is "../", which is correct.

dropped.summary: robotsRe's `<meta\s+name="robots"` misses gnoweb's tag if the attributes are ordered otherwise, leaving two contradicting robots metas
dropped.settled_by: grep -rn robots gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/: head.html:38 `<meta name="robots" content="index, follow" />` and redirect.html:6 `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` — name is first in both, so the regex matches and the branch is live, not dead.

dropped.settled_by: main.go:141 `writeFile(filepath.Join(cfg.out, "index.html"), Index(plan, c))` writes that file at the output root before renderBase runs, so the target resolves for both the prefixed and unprefixed crawls.

dropped.summary: waitReady's url.JoinPath drops the leading slash and requests a relative path
dropped.settled_by: url.JoinPath on a base with an empty EscapedPath takes the relative branch and strips the leading slash from path.Join, but URL.String() re-adds it when Host is set; the resulting request is http://127.0.0.1:8899/r/x/y. The crawl in tests/b2-lines-r2-help-origin_test.go reached every seed through that path.

dropped.summary: attrRe rewrites href/src occurrences inside the $source view's rendered code, corrupting the displayed source
dropped.settled_by: chroma's HTML formatter escapes the double quote, so a source line reading href="/x" reaches the page as href="/x" and never matches attrRe's literal quote.

dropped.summary: slug's maxSlugLen truncation can split a multi-byte rune and emit an invalid UTF-8 directory name
dropped.settled_by: unsafeSeg is [^A-Za-z0-9._-]+, so every non-ASCII byte is replaced with '-' before the truncation; out is pure ASCII by the time out[:maxSlugLen] runs.
